title: US Kids Don't Get the Right Nutrition at Breakfast
paragraphs: In the hurry to get them dressed and out the door, it can be hard to make sure your children eat a healthy breakfast. And in the US, one in five parents admit that what their kids eat often doesn't meet nutrition goals.
This is what a survey of around 1,000 parents of kids aged 6 to 12 by the CS Mott Children's Hospital in Michigan found.

Many American kids don't even eat breakfast at home. Sixty-eight percent of parents said their kids usually eat breakfast at home — but 23% said they get breakfast at school, and 5% reported that their child usually eats something on the way. Four percent said their kids usually don't eat breakfast at all!
And not all breakfasts are equal. The children's hospital says kids need a breakfast that offers a mix of protein and fiber, with very little added sugar.
But only 39% of parents said their children's breakfasts include protein four or five days a week, while 18% said their kids get protein one day a week or less.
As for fiber, 37% of parents said they manage to include it in their kids' breakfasts four or five days a week. But 20% said their kids get fiber one day a week or less.
And just 34% of parents said their kids eat breakfasts low in added sugar four or five days a week, with 19% only managing it one day or less.
Parents who say their children usually choose breakfast for themselves also generally report fewer days when their kids have breakfasts with protein and fiber and low added sugar.

The children's hospital recommends that parents find healthy breakfast options that will fit into their family's schedule — and that parents should, when they can, eat with their kids to teach them good eating habits.
